facts.text: MHW-RTG Nuclear Power Boom was deployed at Interstellar Space (Beyond Heliopause) during Voyager Interstellar Mission in 1977.
facts.source: DOE / GE Space Division RTG Operations Handbook

facts.text: Three Multi-Hundred-Watt Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators stacked on a deployable fiberglass boom, generating electricity from the radioactive decay heat of plutonium-238 dioxide spheres.
facts.source: DOE / GE Space Division RTG Operations Handbook

facts.text: Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Demonstrated record-breaking thermocouple longevity, reliably powering spacecraft electronics for over four decades without moving parts or servicing.
A permanent human and robotic monument celebrating space exploration on the Moon.

scenes.kids: I am MHW-RTG Nuclear Power Boom. I arrived here at Interstellar Space (Beyond Heliopause) in 1977.
scenes.explorer: MHW-RTG Nuclear Power Boom, Voyager Interstellar Mission: deployed at Interstellar Space (Beyond Heliopause) in 1977.

scenes.kids: Take a look at how I was built. Every part of me had a special purpose.
scenes.explorer: Three Multi-Hundred-Watt Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators stacked on a deployable fiberglass boom, generating electricity from the radioactive decay heat of plutonium-238 dioxide spheres.

scenes.kids: Out here, there is no air or weather like on Earth, so I had to work smoothly in the cold.
scenes.explorer: Designed to withstand radiation, cosmic dust, and extreme temperature swings without failing.

scenes.kids: Demonstrated record-breaking thermocouple longevity, reliably powering spacecraft electronics for over four decades without moving parts or servicing.
scenes.explorer: Demonstrated record-breaking thermocouple longevity, reliably powering spacecraft electronics for over four decades without moving parts or servicing.

scenes.kids: I am still working out here every single day, listening and measuring.
scenes.explorer: Fate: operational on surface. Position recorded at coordinates [-3.2, -2.4].

scenes.kids: Everything I learned showed humanity how to explore deeper into space.
scenes.explorer: A milestone in planetary science and permanent historical artifact.
